description: S9.1 (sprint-2-behavioral-spec.md:34-38) states the helper is called `given (privateKey, payload, storeDeps)` — three positional-sounding arguments — and never mentions an injectable clock. But the actual RED test on disk, spawn-register.test.js:42, calls `registerSpawn({ privateKey: KEY, payload: p, storeDeps: stub.deps, now: clock })` — a single options object with a FOURTH `now` parameter that 1b's own S9.3 proof line requires ('injected clock'). 1a also never specifies the return contract; the test asserts `result.message` and `result.signature` (spawn-register.test.js:42-45) — a shape 1a text never commits to. Two builders reading only 1a (without the pre-existing test file) could reasonably implement a different call signature (positional args, no `now` injection point) or a different/no return value, and would fail the actual RED tests.

evidence.snippet: The spawn-register helper `_lib/spawn-register.js` SHALL, given `(privateKey, payload, storeDeps)` ...
